meta.title: Safety demo scenarios
meta.description: Explicitly labelled fictional scenarios used by the Safety Center explanation, the backend tests and the professor demo guide. The scoring rules themselves are NOT stored here — they live in backend/app/services/safety.py so data and rules stay separate.
meta.disclaimer: Fictional demonstration data. No real people, bank accounts, cards, UPI identifiers, PINs or OTPs are represented here.

records.title: High-value payment to a never-seen-before merchant
records.description: A single ₹8,999 payment at 1:12 AM to a merchant that has no history in this account. Illustrates the unusual-amount rule.
records.teaching_note: Three independent rules fire on one payment; each is explained in plain English.

records.title: Burst of payments within one hour
records.description: Three debits (₹8,999, ₹2,499, ₹999) recorded within 14 minutes at night — the pattern account-draining attacks produce.
records.teaching_note: Burst detection is time-window based and independent of merchant or amount.

records.title: Transaction explicitly marked in the demo dataset
records.description: demo_risk_flag=true on txn_010 with an explanation string. Shows how an upstream warning (here: the dataset itself) is surfaced with full attribution.
records.teaching_note: The flag alone contributes 40 points and always quotes its stored reason.

records.title: Ordinary payment that must NOT be treated as fraud
records.description: A ₹140 chai purchase at 9:12 AM through UPI. No rule triggers; the demo proves ordinary payments never appear in the alert list.
records.teaching_note: A safety system that flags everything teaches users to ignore it.
